units.context: Scenario: Health · Lesson: Emergency Situations · grammar (让 + Person + Verb Phrase)
units.source: "让" before a person and verb means "have/let [person] do [verb]" - "请让他躺下" means "please have him lie down".
units.translation: "让" antes de una persona y un verbo significa "hacer que/dejar que [persona] haga [verbo]": "请让他躺下" significa "por favor haz que se acueste".

units.context: Scenario: Health · Lesson: Emergency Situations · grammar (让 + Person + Verb Phrase)
units.source: Confusing 让 (let/have someone do) with 叫 (to call/summon) - both can mean "tell someone to", but 让 is more neutral/permissive.
units.translation: Confundir 让 (dejar/hacer que alguien haga algo) con 叫 (llamar/convocar): ambos pueden significar "decirle a alguien que haga algo", pero 让 es más neutral/permisivo.

units.context: Scenario: Health · Lesson: Emergency Situations · grammar example (让 + Person + Verb Phrase)
units.translation: Por favor haz que se acueste.

units.context: Scenario: Health · Lesson: Emergency Situations · grammar example (让 + Person + Verb Phrase)

units.context: Scenario: Health · Lesson: Emergency Situations · grammar example (让 + Person + Verb Phrase)
